messages.author: 5c7a7c467622edff
messages.subject: Manipulating density object aesthetics
parts:
I am still green with R. I am trying to plot a density object generated by the R "Sparr" Package in Ggplot:

dens<- bivariate.density(pointcase, pilotH=diff(range(pointcase$x))/30, res = 120, edgeCorrect = TRUE) 

So far I have used :

plot(dens,  col = colorRampPalette(c("white", "yellow", "red"))(14), alpha = seq(.15,.45))

but I wish to enhance the display, to get something akin to what this stat_density function produces:

stat_density2d(aes(x = X, y = Y, bw=1, fill = ..level.., alpha = ..level.., adjust=0.25), data = data, size = 0.01,  bins = 14,  geom = "polygon", colour = "grey80") +
scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow", high = "red") + scale_alpha(range = c(.15, .45)

Any kind of help is much welcome and appreciated, thanks!!

Lucy

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Manipulating density object aesthetics
parts:
Hi Lucy,

In the future you should post with a reproducible example so that
people can run your code and see what you're trying to do. Since you
didn't include the data for your example I just used the data returned
by example(bivariate.density). There was some work involved in getting
this right; I tried to document the process so you could follow along.


## make some example object to work with
library(sparr)
example(bivariate.density)

## lookup the docs in ?bivariate.density to figure out what is in the result
## format data for ggplot2, following example at
## http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/stat_density2d.html
dens <- data.frame(expand.grid(x = ch.lar.density$X,
y = ch.lar.density$Y),
z = as.vector(ch.lar.density$Zm))
## was having a hard time with filling unclosed polygons, so cheat
## (not sure this is the best way)
dens[is.na(dens$z), "z"] <- min(dens$z, na.rm = TRUE)

## get the data for the enclosing area
bnd <- data.frame(ch.lar.density$WIN$bdry[[1]][c("x", "y")])

## plot it
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(dens, aes(x = x, y = y))

p + geom_polygon(aes(z = z,
fill = ..level..,
alpha = ..level..),
stat="contour",
size = 0.01,
color="grey80") +
geom_path(data = bnd) +
scale_fill_gradient("level", low = "yellow", high = "red") +
scale_alpha("level", range = c(.15, .45), guide=FALSE)
